expected_skill_registry_entries.statement: FIELD REINTERPRETATION: `abrogator` carries the coordination connector, `ism_marking` the observed case of the joined-to element (head), `khabar_marking` the observed case of the joined element (conjunct). Nothing here is an abrogator and nothing governs anything
the checked relation is INHERITANCE: the conjunct copies the case the head already bears, so a lane is consistent exactly when both observed markings equal the lane's declared case
the consumer CHECKS supplied markings; it never assigns case, never repairs the text, and never decides which element is the head when attachment is ambiguous
a mismatch is a violation_candidate routed to review, because the classic error is giving the conjunct a case of its own
either marking unknown -> abstain marking_unknown; a connector outside the declared inventory -> abstain out_of_regime

a connector whose reading here is NOT coordination (the adversative item once an attached pronoun makes it an abrogator, or any clause-level use with no case to copy) is declared non-governing and abstains

ENCODING LIMIT (recorded, not hidden): the registered analyzer compares each slot against a CONSTANT, so a lane can only pin one case. Every connector in fact joins a head in any case; the lane a connector sits in here is a pack-encoding artifact that fixes which case this unit checks it at, and is NOT a claim about the connector. The repair is a generic head/dependent capability, which is exactly why this canonical unit exists
the six-connector inventory is a teaching core, not the traditional inventory; and each connector has documented non-coordinating uses that this unit does not adjudicate
